actual: cleanup-after-merge is safe for one target but large authorized cleanup requires one process per worktree. Each invocation repeats fetch origin --prune and PR/remote reads, while timed-out git ls-remote or git push on Windows can leave git-remote-https descendants alive and the parent workflow blocked for several minutes. In a 101-target cleanup this created dominant network latency and required exact process-tree recovery. Add a bounded bulk cleanup path that performs one shared preflight fetch and reuses validated PR receipts without weakening per-target worktree, artifact, process, remote-SHA, or four-state checks. Ensure subprocess timeout terminates the owned Windows process tree and records a structured per-target failure while continuing independent targets.
closure_requirements: Keep BUG JSON and GitHub Issue synchronized.
